ops.title: Post-freeze daemon-squat recovery
ops.body:
After a machine freeze (e.g. the fork-bomb / holder-spawn-storm incident — `ccn doc search "fork storm"`),
all ccp sessions can show **stale / no-auth** with this exact signature — and it is NOT credential loss:

- `~/.cc-pool/daemon.log` floods with `error: another cc-pool daemon at the same version is already running`
  (observed 4727+). Cause: an **orphaned `ccp daemon`** (re-parented to PID 1, or spawned by a sibling
  `claude` session via a `ccp` autostart) **squats `~/.cc-pool/daemon.sock`**, so the brew/launchd
  KeepAlive agent `homebrew.mxcl.cc-pool` can't bind and **flaps** (`launchctl print … runs=N, last exit
  code=1`; `brew services list` → `error`).
- The wedged daemon's usage-poll loop is dead → `status.json` shows every account
  `has_usage:false, stale:true`. The `oauth usage HTTP 401` lines are a **chronic red herring** (predate
  the incident by weeks; decreasing) and the `security … exit status 51` (`errSecAuthFailed`) is a one-off
  locked-keychain blip — neither is the cause.
- The host's process-query subsystem (`sysmond`) wedges too: `ps -U $UID` returns nothing, `pgrep` exits 3
  (WindowServer is fine — pgrep is just blind). Load climbs from accumulated D-state procs stuck on wedged
  fuse-t I/O. Killing the runaway ccp procs and dropping load un-sticks sysmond on its own.

**Credentials are intact throughout** — they live ONLY in the per-account Keychain item
`Claude Code-credentials-<sha256(NFC(configDir))[:8]>` (no `.credentials.json`, no `acct-NN.private/` on a
desktop box); the overlay symlink/fuse flip is NOT on the auth path. Verify (no secret printed):
`security find-generic-password -s "Claude Code-credentials-<hash>" -a $USER`  (exit 0 = present & ok).

## Recovery (no reboot needed)

1. `brew services stop cc-pool` — boot out the KeepAlive loop FIRST (else killing the squatter just lets
   launchd grab the freed socket).
2. Find PIDs with `lsof -n -- ~/.cc-pool/daemon.sock ~/.cc-pool/mounts.sock` (ps is blind). `SIGTERM` the
   orphan daemon + mount-holder. **Never `-9` the holder** (holder-kill-meltdown: wedged fuse-t mounts +
   heavy lsof exhausted the process table and froze the machine); TERM suffices when no fuse mounts exist
   (all converged to symlink). D-state remnants are harmless.
3. `brew services start cc-pool` → launchd daemon binds; `brew services list` flips to `started`,
   `ps … ppid=1`, log shows `daemon … started`. Watch for a sibling `claude` session racing to re-spawn a
   squatter in the gap — kill it so launchd wins the socket.
4. Verify: `ccp status` shows live 5h/7d usage, `status.json` `has_usage:true`, daemon serves selects.

`mount holder unreachable` after restart is benign while accounts are on the symlink overlay (DB
`accounts.overlay_kind=symlink`, `meta.overlay_kind=nfs`); symlink is the more stable state — only
`ccp fuse enable` brings the fuse-t mirror back, and watch for churn.

**Underlying bug worth a minimal fix:** a transient freeze becomes a *persistent* outage purely because an
orphaned non-launchd daemon can squat the socket while KeepAlive flaps forever. A startup check that evicts
a non-launchd socket squatter (or makes the KeepAlive daemon reclaim a stale-owned socket) would make this
self-heal. Related daemon-churn family: the fuse-t "not responding/alive again" force-unmount churn.
ops.when: When troubleshooting cc-pool daemon flaps, socket conflicts, 'another daemon already running' floods, stale/no-auth across all accounts, or working on the daemon/KeepAlive/mount-holder lifecycle
